setup.title: Set up the GitHub sign-in
setup.intro: The CMS needs a GitHub App to sign editors in. Check the list below, then create the App.
setup.callbackHint: The GitHub App uses this URL to send the editor back after sign-in. The Create button sets it for you.
setup.devNote: In development, the Create button saves the keys in your .env file. Restart the dev server after it.

ready.title: The GitHub sign-in is ready
ready.description: The GitHub App is set up. Editors can sign in.

repo.title: The content repository is set
repo.fix: Set PLUTO_GITHUB_REPO to owner/name, for example acme/site.

sessionPassword.title: The session password is set
sessionPassword.fix: Set NUXT_PLUTO_GITHUB_SESSION_PASSWORD to a random text of 32 characters or more. The Create button makes one.

appId.title: The GitHub App ID is set
appId.fix: Set NUXT_PLUTO_GITHUB_APP_ID. The Create button sets it.

clientId.title: The client ID is set
clientId.fix: Set NUXT_PLUTO_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. The Create button sets it.

clientSecret.title: The client secret is set
clientSecret.fix: Set NUXT_PLUTO_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET. The Create button sets it.

privateKey.title: The private key is valid
privateKey.fix: Set NUXT_PLUTO_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY to the PEM key, or to its base64. The Create button sets it.

installation.title: The App is installed on the repository
installation.fix: Install the GitHub App on the content repository, then check again.

settings.title: GitHub
settings.intro: The GitHub App that signs editors in and saves their changes to the repository.

start.title: Create the GitHub App
start.body: You go to GitHub to confirm a new App named "{name}". Nothing is created until you confirm. You can change the name there.

result.title: The GitHub App is created
result.intro: The App "{name}" is ready. Do these three steps.
result.secretNote: This page shows secrets. The site does not store them. Close this page when you are done.
result.step1Prod: Copy this block. Paste it in the environment variables of your host.
result.step1Dev: The block below has the same values that the site wrote into your .env file.
result.envSaved: The values are saved in the .env file.
result.envFailed: The site could not write the .env file. Copy the block below and paste it in .env.
result.envNotIgnored: Warning: .gitignore does not ignore .env. Do not commit this file.
result.step2: Install the App on the repository
result.step2Body: Choose the content repository only. The App cannot save posts until you install it.
result.step3Prod: Paste the block in your host (on Vercel: Settings, Environment Variables, then paste the block). Redeploy the site. Then sign in.
result.step3Dev: Restart the dev server so it reads the .env file. Then sign in.

test.body: This is a test email from {siteName}. You can read it, so your email setup works.
test.hint: You can close this email. Nothing else is needed.
test.selfTitle: Send a test email to yourself
test.selfDescription: This shows that the key works.
test.selfRule: Until you verify a domain, Resend delivers only to the email address of your Resend account. Use that address here.
test.anyoneTitle: Send a test email to anyone
test.anyoneDescription: This shows that the verified domain and the From address work.
test.anyoneHelp: Use an address that is not yours, if you can.
test.sentHint: Check the inbox. It can take a minute. Look in the spam folder too.
test.sentDev: Development mode: nothing was sent. Read the email in the server console.
test.senderRuleTitle: Resend sends test emails to your own address only
test.senderRuleBody: Resend sends from its test address only to the email of your Resend account. Send the test to that address. To send to other people, add and verify a domain in step 4, and set the From address in step 5.
test.failed: Could not send the test email
test.lockedFrom: Set the From address first (step 5), and restart the server.

page.title: Email
page.intro: Set up the email that this site sends, such as invitations. Follow the steps in order. Each step tells you what to do.

status.title: Email status
status.loadFailed: Could not read the email status
status.fromEmpty: Not set (uses the Resend test address)
status.noteMailpit: Development mode: emails go to your Mailpit inbox. Nothing leaves your computer.
status.noteLogOnly: Development mode: emails print in the server console. Nothing is sent. Add a Resend API key to send real emails.
status.noteNotConfigured: This site cannot send email yet. Follow the steps below.

account.title: Create a Resend account
account.description: Resend sends the emails. The free plan is enough to start.
account.body: Sign up with the email address you want to use for tests. Resend lets a new account send test emails to that address only, until you verify a domain.

key.title: Add your API key
key.description: The key lets this site send through your Resend account. It stays in the server, never in the browser.
key.stepCreate: In Resend, create an API key with full access at
key.stepAdd: Add this line to the environment of the server. On your computer, use the .env file. On a host, use its environment settings.
key.envHint: Replace re_your_key_here with your key. Pluto never stores the key and never shows it again.
key.full: The key works and has full access
key.fullHint: You can add a domain in step 4.
key.sending: The key works and can only send emails
key.sendingHint: You can send test emails. To add a domain here, use a key with full access. Or add the domain in the Resend dashboard.
key.invalidHint: Check that you copied the whole key, and that it is not deleted in Resend.
key.missing: The server has no key yet
key.missingHint: Add the line above to the server environment, restart the server, and check again.
key.failedHint: Resend did not answer as expected. Try again in a moment.

domain.title: Add your domain
domain.description: Resend sends from your own domain after you verify it.
domain.lockedKey: Add and check a key with full access first (step 2).
domain.lockedSending: This key can only send emails. Use a key with full access to add a domain here.
domain.existing: Use a domain from your Resend account
domain.name: Domain
domain.recordsHint: Add these DNS records at the company that manages your domain. Then press Verify. It can take a few minutes, and up to a few hours.
domain.verifiedHint: Set the From address in step 5.
domain.failedTitle: Resend could not verify the domain
domain.failedHint: A DNS record is wrong or missing. Compare each record with the table, fix it, and press Check again.
domain.timedOutHint: DNS can be slow. Press Check again when you are ready.

from.title: Set the From address
from.description: This is the sender name and address that people see.
from.notVerified: The domain is not verified yet. Resend refuses to send from it until it is.
from.name: Sender name
from.nameHelp: For example the name of your shop.
from.addressInvalid: Use letters, numbers, dots, dashes or plus signs.
from.replyToHelp: Replies go here. Leave it empty to reply to the From address.
from.envHint: Add these lines to the environment of the server, then restart it.

sendingKey.title: Use a sending-only key
sendingKey.description: A key that can only send emails is safer to keep in the server.
sendingKey.alreadySending: The key in the server can already only send emails.
sendingKey.lockedKey: This step needs a key with full access (step 2).
sendingKey.forDomain: The new key can send only from {domain}.
sendingKey.forAccount: The new key can only send emails.
sendingKey.onceBody: Pluto shows the key once and does not keep it. If you close this page, create another key.
sendingKey.next: Replace the key line in the server environment, restart the server, then delete the old full-access key in Resend.
